st.2: It was excavated during 1961–69 by R. S. Bisht.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Kalibangan was excavated (1961–69) by B.B. Lal and B.K. Thapar; R.S. Bisht excavated Dholavira.

st.1: Two rows of six granaries each
st.2: A dockyard

x: Finds 1, 3 and 4 come from Harappa (two rows of six granaries, Cemeteries H and R-37, wheat and barley in a wooden mortar). The dockyard is at Lothal, not Harappa.
All three statements are correct: Kot Diji has pre-Harappan and Harappan levels, Sohgaura is a Mauryan copper-plate site, and Surkotada and Desalpur are Harappan sites in Kachchh.

st.2: Goods moved in bullock carts with spoked wheels.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Harappan carts had solid wheels, not spoked wheels.

st.1: It was used for beads, bangles, amulets and small figurines.

x: All four statements are correct: faience, the world's first glazed ware, was ground silica glazed blue-green, used for beads, bangles, amulets and figurines, and its link with mosaic glass is an early clue to glass-making.

st.3: An IIT Kharagpur study found continuous low rainfall for about 900 years.

x: All three statements are correct: the 4.2 ka event was a sharp monsoon weakening, linked also to the fall of Akkad and Old Kingdom Egypt, and the IIT Kharagpur study found about 900 years of low rainfall.

st.2: Gunadhya wrote the Brihatkatha in Paishachi Prakrit.

x: All three statements are correct: Hala composed the Gathasaptasati in Maharashtri Prakrit, Gunadhya wrote the Brihatkatha in Paishachi, and the Harshacharita calls Yajna Sri Satakarni 'Trisamudradheesvara'.

st.3: The Vidatha is the assembly mentioned least often in the Rigveda.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Vidatha is the most often mentioned assembly (122 times) and the first to disappear.

st.2: Burnt bricks were commonly used.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: burnt bricks were not common in Later Vedic settlements; houses were of mud-brick and wattle-and-daub.

st.3: Their head (jetthaka or pamukha) was elected or hereditary.

x: All three statements are correct: guilds fixed prices and wages, followed their own shreni-dharma, and had elected or hereditary heads (jetthaka / pamukha).

st.3: Myanmar is one of the principal homes of Mahayana Buddhism.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Myanmar is a home of Hinayana (Theravada), not Mahayana.

st.3: Uddeshika stupas are commemorative and contain no relics.

x: All three statements are correct: Dhatugarbha stupas hold bodily relics, Paribhogika stupas hold objects used by the Buddha, and Uddeshika stupas are commemorative with no relics.

st.2: The Amaravati School of art is noted for its red sandstone.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Amaravati School is noted for white limestone (red sandstone is Mathura's).

st.3: Ikshvaku royal women such as Chantisiri and Bodhisiri patronised Buddhism at Nagarjunakonda.

x: All three statements are correct: Rayalaseema was a Jain corridor on the Bhadrabahu–Chandragupta route, Mahapadma Nanda is said to have spread Jainism in Andhra, and the Ikshvaku queens backed Buddhism at Nagarjunakonda.

st.3: Bhadrabahu survived Mahavira and became the first Thera (head of the Sangha).

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: only Arya Sudharma survived Mahavira and became the first Thera; Bhadrabahu was the sixth Thera.

st.2: The Pandya kingdom lay within the Mauryan Empire.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Pandya kingdom lay outside the Mauryan Empire, named in the edicts as a neighbour.
Both statements are correct: Brahmanical sources link Maurya with the Shudra woman Mura, while Buddhist and Jain sources make Chandragupta a Kshatriya of the Moriya clan.

st.2: Mining, salt and liquor were left wholly to private guilds.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: mining, salt and liquor were state monopolies, not left to private guilds.

st.2: Chandragupta II did not annex the Vakataka kingdom; he allied with it by marrying his daughter Prabhavati to Rudrasena II.

x: Both statements are correct: Prabhavati Gupta ruled as regent after Rudrasena II died, and Chandragupta II made the Vakatakas an ally by marriage instead of annexing them.

st.2: The shift to South-East Asian trade revived the economy of North India.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the shift to South-East Asian trade did not revive the North Indian economy, which declined after the loss of the Roman market.

st.1: Gupta silver coins began under Chandragupta II, after his conquest of the Western Kshatrapas.

x: All three statements are correct: Chandragupta II began Gupta silver coinage after defeating the Sakas, modelling it on Saka silver issues, and the largest Gupta hoard is from Bayana.

st.2: Malik Muhammad Jayasi wrote Padmavat in Persian in 1540.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Jayasi wrote Padmavat (1540) in Awadhi, not Persian.

st.2: He received the title Ulugh Khan from Iltutmish.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Balban got the title Ulugh Khan from Nasiruddin Mahmud, not Iltutmish.

st.2: Ushr was paid by non-Muslim cultivators.
st.3: Ghari and charai were sharia taxes.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: ushr was a land tax on Muslim cultivators. Statement 3 is wrong: ghari (house tax) and charai (grazing tax) were non-sharia taxes.

st.2: He wrote his Tarikh-i-Ferishta (Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi) at the court of Ibrahim Adil Shah II of Bijapur.

x: All three statements are correct: Ferishta, born at Astarabad, wrote at the Bijapur court of Ibrahim Adil Shah II, and calls Telangana 'Tilang' while describing the fall of Warangal (1323).
All three statements are correct: chehra was the descriptive roll, Akbar revived dagh and chehra, and the walashahi were the emperor's bodyguards.

st.3: Mirabai, a Rathore princess of Merta, was married to Rana Sanga of Mewar.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Mirabai was married to Bhoj Raj, the son of Rana Sanga, not to Rana Sanga himself.

st.3: He was the disciple of Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki.

x: All three statements are correct: Baba Farid was born at Kothewal, his verses are in the Guru Granth Sahib, and he was the disciple of Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki (Nizamuddin Auliya was Farid's own disciple).

st.2: Under the Indian Councils Act, 1861, the Viceroy could issue an ordinance only with the concurrence of the legislative council.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Viceroy could issue ordinances without the council's concurrence in an emergency, valid for six months.

st.4: The Maratha chief Morari Rao fought on the English side.

x: All four statements are correct: Clive took Arcot (1751) with about 210 men, held it about 53 days, beat Raja Sahib at Arni and Kaveripak, and Morari Rao's Marathas helped the English.

st.4: The Treaty of Pondicherry ended the Second Carnatic War with a decisive French victory.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the Treaty of Pondicherry left the Second Carnatic War inconclusive, and Dupleix was recalled.

st.1: The Andhra Mahasabha at Nandyal that approved the name Rayalaseema was presided over by Dr S. Radhakrishnan.

x: All three statements are correct: the Nandyal Andhra Mahasabha (1928) was presided over by Dr S. Radhakrishnan, the Nizam ceded the four districts on 12 October 1800, and Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao proposed the name.

st.3: He died in Ranchi jail on 9 June 1900.

x: All three statements are correct: Birsa Munda was born on 15 November 1875, captured in Jamkopai forest on 3 February 1900, and died in Ranchi jail on 9 June 1900.

st.1: The first census of 1872, held under him, was non-synchronous and did not cover all areas at the same time.

x: All three statements are correct: the 1872 census was non-synchronous, the 1870 Resolution began financial decentralisation, and Rajkot and Mayo Colleges were set up for princes.

st.3: The First Law Commission under Macaulay to codify Indian laws was set up in 1834.

x: All three statements are correct: Macaulay became the fourth (Law) Member, the post is the origin of the Law Ministry, and the First Law Commission came in 1834.

st.3: The rise in litigation after 1793 was mainly due to its land provisions.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: litigation rose after 1793 because of Cornwallis' judicial reforms (no court fees, separate civil courts), not the land provisions.

st.1: Jawaharlal Nehru called it "thoroughly rotten, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable".

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: 'thoroughly rotten, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable' was Jinnah's verdict; Nehru called it a machine with strong brakes but no engine.

st.2: The Tattvabodhini Sabha was established after the Brahmo Sabha.

x: All three statements are correct: the Brahmo Sabha came in 1828, the Tattvabodhini Sabha in 1839, and the Ramakrishna Mission (1897) after the Arya Samaj (1875).

st.3: Ambedkar refused to sign the Poona Pact.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Ambedkar signed the Poona Pact (1932), giving up separate electorates for reserved seats.

st.1: In 'Thoughts on Linguistic States' (1955) Ambedkar accepted 'one language, one state'.

x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Ambedkar accepted 'one state, one language' but rejected 'one language, one state'.

st.4: The Ramakrishna Math and the Ramakrishna Mission are legally and financially separate bodies.

st.3: Tilak's league worked in Maharashtra (except Bombay city), Karnataka, the Central Provinces and Berar.

x: All four statements are correct: Tilak's league was launched at Belgaum and covered Maharashtra outside Bombay city, Karnataka, CP and Berar; Besant's, at Adyar, had about 200 branches.

st.3: Gandhi's speech at Vijayawada on 8 April 1919 was translated by Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao.

x: All three statements are correct: the 6 April hartal was peaceful in the Andhra towns, the Andhra Patrika and Krishna Patrika opposed the Act, and Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao translated Gandhi's Vijayawada speech.

st.3: Irwin agreed to return confiscated lands that had not yet been sold to third parties.

x: All three statements are correct: the pact was signed on 5 March 1931, Sapru and Jayakar mediated, and only confiscated land not yet sold to third parties was to be returned.

st.3: Commutation of the death sentences of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru

x: Items 2 and 4 are correct. Item 1 is wrong: Irwin refused a public inquiry into police excesses. Item 3 is wrong: the pact did not commute the death sentences of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru.

st.2: He declared 'Sampoorna Kranti' at the Gandhi Maidan, Patna, on 5 June 1974.
st.3: He served for a time as a member of the Viceroy's Executive Council.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: JP never sat on the Viceroy's Executive Council; he was a socialist leader outside government.

st.3: Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma was the first woman jailed in the movement.

x: All three statements are correct: Bezawada Gopala Reddy abolished the municipality, Pisapati Narayana Sastri wrote Chirala Perala Vanavasam, and Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma was the first woman jailed (Duvvuri Subbamma was arrested later).

st.3: Vedavanam, T. Prakasam's house that served as a satyagraha centre, was in Madras.

st.3: Bhairavakonda, a Saiva centre with eight rock-cut caves, is in Nellore district.

x: All three statements are correct: Santamula gave gold, cows and ploughs and agraharas to northern Brahmins, and spent part of his revenue on tanks and canals (not on overseas colonies).

st.3: Nagavarma II wrote the Kavyavalokana in Kannada.

x: All four statements are correct: Bilhana likens Vikramaditya VI's reign to Ramarajya, the Manasollasa is a 100-chapter encyclopaedia, Nagavarma II wrote the Kavyavalokana in Kannada, and vachanas are linked with Basavanna, Allama and Akka.

st.3: Magani was irrigated wet land and Metta was rain-fed dry land.

x: All four statements are correct: ari was about one-sixth of the produce, payers were Arigapulu and collectors Kolakandru, Magani was wet and Metta dry land, and Dashabandhamu land was tax-free.

st.4: Narsapuram in the Godavari delta was the chief shipbuilding port of the Golconda kingdom.

x: All four statements are correct: diamonds were traded at Moti Darwaza and polished at Karwan, the Golconda Blue weighs 23.24 carats, Machilipatnam was famous for muslin and Kalamkari, and Narsapuram was the chief shipbuilding port.

st.1: Tax farmers were called Mahasibs.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Mahasibs were in charge of public morals; revenue was collected through tax farmers who bid for the rights.

st.2: Sewell recorded seven local traditions of the founding of Vijayanagara.

x: All three statements are correct: 'A Forgotten Empire' (1900) carries Paes and Nuniz in English, Sewell recorded seven founding traditions, and the Nellore inscription first calls Harihara I king.

st.1: Prataparudra ascended the throne after Rudramadevi.

x: All three statements are correct: Prataparudra succeeded Rudramadevi, Mahadeva came between Rudradeva and Ganapatideva, and Rudramadevi succeeded Ganapatideva in 1262.

st.2: Pillalamarri and Nagulapadu are in Suryapet district.
st.4: The Pillalamarri paintings paved the way for the Mughal miniature style.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the Pillalamarri paintings led to the Lepakshi style, not the Mughal miniature.

st.3: At Pattadakal, the Papanatha temple is in the Nagara form and the Virupaksha in the Dravida form.

x: All three statements are correct: the vahana and dhvaja stand axially before the sanctum, a trikutalaya has three shrines as in the Thousand Pillar temple, and at Pattadakal Papanatha is Nagara while Virupaksha is Dravida.

st.4: Unnava Lakshmibayamma ran the monthly Andhra Mahila.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the Telugu monthly Andhra Mahila was run by Durgabai Deshmukh, not Unnava Lakshmibayamma.

st.3: Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya was the secretary of the Rama Mohana Library, Vijayawada (1911), which later became the central library of Andhra.

x: All four statements are correct: the Gautami Granthalayam was formed by a merger in 1898, Kallakuri Narasimha founded the Rayakuduru and Kopalle libraries, Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya was secretary of the Rama Mohana Library, and the Andhra Council of Research was at Kovvur.

st.2: The Chunduru massacre took place on 6 August 1991 in Guntur district.

x: All three statements are correct: Karamchedu was on 17 July 1985 in Prakasam, Chunduru on 6 August 1991 in Guntur, and after Karamchedu Dalits formed independent Dalit Mahasabhas.

st.3: Kashi was ruled by the Pradyota dynasty until Magadha annexed it.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Kashi was ruled by the Brahmadatta dynasty until Kosala annexed it (the Pradyotas ruled Avanti).

st.2: The Kushanas defeated the Chinese force of Pan Chao in 86 AD.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Kushanas were defeated by the Chinese general Pan Chao, not the other way round.

st.2: Nedunjeliyan was one of the seven vallals.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Nedunjeliyan was a Pandya king (victor of Talaiyalanganam), not one of the seven vallals (patron chieftains).

st.3: Mayurasharman, a student insulted at the Kanchi Ghatika, went on to found the Kadamba kingdom.

x: All three statements are correct: Pallava ghatikas taught in Sanskrit, Jayasimha I set up a ghatika at Asanapura, and Mayurasharman founded the Kadamba kingdom (Talagunda inscription).

st.2: Vishnugopa faced the invasion of Samudragupta.

x: Both statements are correct: Kanchi came under the Pallavas under Sivaskandavarman, and Vishnugopa of Kanchi faced Samudragupta's invasion (Simhavishnu came much later).

st.2: The Vimal Vasahi is dedicated to Neminatha.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Vimal Vasahi is dedicated to Rishabha (Adinatha); the Luna Vasahi is the Neminatha temple.

st.2: The National Policy for Senior Citizens, 2011 held that destitution among the elderly was confined to the urban areas.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2011 policy drew attention to the rural poor elderly, who form most of the aged, and not to the urban elderly alone.

st.1: The Special Marriage Act, 1954 provides for inter-religious civil marriage before a Marriage Officer, but registration under it is optional.
st.2: Divorce under the Special Marriage Act, 1954 is provided by Section 13.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: registration is compulsory under the Special Marriage Act (the certificate is the registration). Statement 2 is wrong: divorce under the Special Marriage Act is in Section 27 (Section 13 is the Hindu Marriage Act's).

st.1: The Khasis and Garos of Meghalaya and the Nagas of Nagaland are matrilineal.

st.4: The Namboodiris of Kerala are a matrilineal Brahmin community.

st.3: Kshatriyaisation among Marathas, Jats and Yadavs is seen as breaking down the caste hierarchy.

st.3: Delhi was the largest urban agglomeration of India in Census 2001.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Greater Mumbai was the largest urban agglomeration in 2001 (Mumbai > Kolkata > Delhi).

st.2: Giddens defined a minority as a group set apart by race, nationality, religion or language and regarded as different by itself and others.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: this definition of a minority is Arnold Rose's; Giddens stressed disadvantage, solidarity and isolation.

st.1: The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 declares all forms of talaq void and illegal.
st.2: Pronouncing instant talaq under the 2019 Act is punishable only with a fine.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Act voids only instant talaq-e-biddat, not all forms of talaq. Statement 2 is wrong: it is punishable with imprisonment up to three years and fine.

st.3: The Haji Ali Dargah case was decided by the Kerala High Court in 2016.

st.2: Only Odisha and Madhya Pradesh are covered.
st.3: The 94th Amendment added Bihar to the list.

st.3: Parents or guardians are punishable even for a first offence.

st.3: Andhra Pradesh's Dokka Seethamma Mid-Day Meal was extended to degree colleges in 2024-25.

st.2: Child Marriage Prohibition Officers are appointed by the Central Government.

st.3: Only senior citizens of BPL families are eligible under it.

st.2: The Rurban Mission revives M.S. Swaminathan's idea of PURA.
st.3: The National Council for Land Reforms (2008) is chaired by the Union Minister of Rural Development.

st.2: Crimes against STs rose by 23.1% in 2024.

st.2: Jains were among the first five minority communities notified in 1993.

st.2: The Provincial Constitution Committee was chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Provincial Constitution Committee was chaired by Sardar Patel; Nehru chaired the Union Constitution and Union Powers Committees.

st.2: The Central Legislative Assembly continued alongside the Constituent Assembly.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Central Legislative Assembly ended, and the Constituent Assembly also sat as the Dominion Legislature.

st.2: The French Constitution is the world's first written Constitution and also the shortest, with 7 Articles.
st.3: The phrase 'procedure established by law' in Article 21 was borrowed from the US Constitution.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the US Constitution (1787) is the first written and the shortest Constitution. Statement 3 is wrong: 'procedure established by law' in Article 21 came from Japan, not the USA ('due process of law').

st.4: The voting age was lowered to 18 years by the 42nd Amendment.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the voting age was lowered to 18 by the 61st Amendment (1988), not the 42nd.

st.2: In Kaushal Kishor (2023), the Supreme Court held these grounds to be only illustrative, so new grounds can be added.
st.3: Sedition is one of the grounds listed in it.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Kaushal Kishor (2023) held the grounds to be exhaustive. Statement 3 is wrong: sedition is not one of the Article 19(2) grounds.

st.2: In May 2026, the Supreme Court said peaceful protesters may occupy public spaces for as long as they choose.
st.3: The right to strike is a Fundamental Right under Article 19(1)(c).

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: on 22 May 2026 the Supreme Court said peaceful protest is everybody's right but must not disturb other citizens or occupy public space. Statement 3 is wrong: the right to strike is not a Fundamental Right (Kameshwar Prasad).

st.2: Aruna Shanbaug (2011) upheld the living will (advance directive).

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the living will was upheld in Common Cause (2018), not in Aruna Shanbaug (2011).

st.2: It extended OBC reservation to promotions as a general rule.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Indra Sawhney held that there would be no reservation in promotions.

st.1: The 27 per cent OBC quota in Central Government posts was given effect by the Rao Government's own order, without any Supreme Court ruling.
st.3: Ashoka Kumar Thakur v. Union of India (2008) upheld the 27 per cent OBC quota under the CEI Act and applied the creamy-layer exclusion to SCs and STs as well.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the V.P. Singh Government's August 1990 order took effect in central posts only from 1993, after Indra Sawhney upheld it. Statement 3 is wrong: Ashoka Kumar Thakur applied the creamy layer to OBCs only, not to SCs and STs.

All four statements are correct: the Legal Services Authorities Act came into force on 9 November 1995, NALSA gives effect to Article 39A, the NSAP meets Article 41, and MGNREGA has been replaced by the VB-G RAM G Act.

st.1: A law violating a Directive Principle can be struck down under Article 13, just like one violating a Fundamental Right.
st.2: Fundamental Rights are positive directions, while Directive Principles are negative restraints on the State.
st.3: Fundamental Rights are described as the ends and Directive Principles as the means.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: only a law violating a Fundamental Right is void under Article 13; Directive Principles are not justiciable. Statement 2 is wrong: Fundamental Rights are negative restraints and Directive Principles positive directions. Statement 3 is wrong: Directive Principles are the ends and Fundamental Rights the means.

st.2: The accounts must be audited only by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Article 243ZM requires audit within six months of the year's close by an auditor or firm from a panel approved by the State, not by the CAG.

st.3: If an Emergency is approved by the Rajya Sabha while the Lok Sabha is dissolved, it need not be placed before the new Lok Sabha.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the new Lok Sabha must approve the Emergency within 30 days of its first sitting.

st.1: It reserves one-third of the seats in the Lok Sabha, the Rajya Sabha and the State Assemblies for women.
st.2: Once in force, the reservation cannot be extended by Parliament.
st.4: The first Women's Reservation Bill was introduced in 1996 and was passed by the Lok Sabha in 2010.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Rajya Sabha is not covered; seats are reserved in the Lok Sabha, the State Assemblies and the Delhi Assembly. Statement 2 is wrong: the reservation runs for 15 years and Parliament may extend it by law. Statement 4 is wrong: the 2010 Bill was passed by the Rajya Sabha, not the Lok Sabha.

st.2: Most Bills were referred to parliamentary committees.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: fewer than one-fifth of Bills went to committees in the Seventeenth Lok Sabha.

st.1: The coalition era (1989–2014) drew the criticism of 'cabinet dictatorship' over Parliament.
st.3: The 'kitchen cabinet' – the PM's informal inner circle – is a body recognised under Article 74.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: 'cabinet dictatorship' is the criticism of single-party majority eras; the coalition era weakened the Cabinet. Statement 3 is wrong: the kitchen cabinet is an informal, extra-constitutional circle with no constitutional status.

st.2: British courts can strike down Acts of Parliament.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: British courts cannot strike down Acts of Parliament, as Parliament is sovereign.

st.2: 'Epistolary jurisdiction' means that only formal writ petitions filed by advocates are treated as petitions.
st.3: Judicial activism emerged in India before the Emergency of 1975.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: epistolary jurisdiction means treating letters, postcards and newspaper reports as petitions. Statement 3 is wrong: judicial activism emerged in India in the mid-1970s, after the Emergency.

st.2: Tribunals replace the High Courts in their fields, and their decisions cannot go before a High Court.
st.3: Parliament can take away judicial review by an amendment under Article 368 passed by a special majority.
st.4: In Madras Bar Association (2021, Nov 2025) the Supreme Court upheld the re-enacted provisions on tribunal members.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: tribunals only supplement the High Courts, and their decisions lie before a High Court bench. Statement 3 is wrong: judicial review is part of the basic structure and cannot be taken away even by amendment. Statement 4 is wrong: the Supreme Court struck down the re-enacted provisions.

st.2: The Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021 dissolved the National Green Tribunal.
st.4: That judgment was delivered by a bench headed by CJI D.Y. Chandrachud.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2021 Act dissolved bodies such as the FCAT and AAT, not the National Green Tribunal. Statement 4 is wrong: the 19 November 2025 judgment was by a bench headed by CJI B.R. Gavai.

st.2: The first Finance Commission was constituted under Article 275.
st.4: The 15th Finance Commission was chaired by Y.V. Reddy.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Finance Commission is constituted under Article 280 (Article 275 deals with grants-in-aid). Statement 4 is wrong: the 15th Finance Commission was chaired by N.K. Singh; Y.V. Reddy chaired the 14th.

st.2: The Selection Committee can choose only from the names shortlisted by the Search Committee.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Selection Committee may also consider persons not shortlisted by the Search Committee.

st.1: The 105th Amendment (2021) took away the power of the States to keep their own lists of SEBCs.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 105th Amendment (2021) restored the States' power to keep their own SEBC lists.

st.2: The first appeal lies to the Central or State Information Commission.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the first appeal lies to a senior officer (First Appellate Authority) in the same public authority; the second appeal goes to the Information Commission.

st.2: The first Lokayukta of integrated Andhra Pradesh was Justice P. Lakshmana Reddy.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the first Lokayukta of integrated AP was Justice A. Sambasiva Rao; P. Lakshmana Reddy was the first of residuary AP (2019).

st.3: Coalition partners at the Centre coordinated through the Inter-State Council, criticised as a 'super-cabinet'.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: partners coordinated through a coordination committee, which critics called a 'super-cabinet', not the Inter-State Council.

st.4: All India Trinamool Congress

x: The DMK, TDP and Samajwadi Party have never been national parties. The All India Trinamool Congress was a recognised national party from 2016 until 2023.

st.1: Women's voter turnout has never exceeded men's in a Lok Sabha election.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: women's turnout exceeded men's for the first time in the 2019 Lok Sabha election.

st.3: An election need be held only when the full five-year term would have ended.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: an election must be held within six months of dissolution (Article 243U).

st.2: It was replaced by the Consumer Protection Act.
st.3: In 1991 its asset limits were abolished, but prior approval for mergers and acquisitions was retained.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the MRTP Act was replaced by the Competition Act, 2002. Statement 3 is wrong: the 1991 reforms removed both the asset limits and the pre-entry curbs on expansion, mergers and acquisitions.

st.3: It targets exports of $2 trillion by 2030 from merchandise alone.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the $2 trillion target for 2030 covers goods and services together, not merchandise alone.

st.2: Forex reserves fell to about $975 million in June 1991, enough for about two months of imports.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: reserves of about $975 million in June 1991 covered only about two weeks of imports.

st.1: The developer pays 40% of the cost during construction and the government's 60% is repaid by semi-annual annuities over about 15 years.
st.2: The developer bears the traffic risk.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the government pays 40% during construction and the developer's 60% is repaid by annuities. Statement 2 is wrong: under HAM the government (NHAI) bears the traffic risk.

st.2: Governance is narrower than government, as it covers only the State.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: governance is wider than government, covering markets and civil society as well as the State.

st.3: About 67% of cases under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code are resolved within 330 days.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: about 67% of IBC cases exceed the 330-day limit.

st.4: The Gujral Doctrine offered goodwill to neighbours in return for reciprocal concessions.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the Gujral Doctrine offered goodwill to neighbours without asking for reciprocity.

st.1: Andhra Pradesh plans to divert 200 TMC of Polavaram flood water through it.

x: All three statements are correct: AP plans to divert 200 TMC of Polavaram flood water, Telangana withdrew its Supreme Court petition in January 2026, and the CWC Chairman's committee first met on 30 January 2026.

st.4: Krishna was the lowest-poverty district of AP.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: West Godavari (2.42%) had the lowest poverty in AP, ahead of Guntur and Krishna.

st.3: Women's share of parliamentary seats is an indicator of its empowerment dimension.

x: All four statements are correct: 0 means equality, reproductive health uses MMR and adolescent births, parliamentary seats fall in the empowerment dimension, and India rose from 108th to 102nd.

st.3: The IHDI captures intragenerational inequality while the PHDI captures intergenerational inequality.

x: All three statements are correct: HDR 2021/22 described a new uncertainty complex, the HDI–IHDI gap is the loss due to inequality, and the IHDI is intragenerational while the PHDI is intergenerational.

st.3: The Planetary pressures-adjusted HDI adjusts the HDI for inequality in income.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the PHDI (HDR 2020) adjusts the HDI for CO2 emissions and material footprint; inequality is the IHDI's adjustment.

st.3: AMRUT 2.0 seeks universal water supply only in the 500 AMRUT cities.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: AMRUT 2.0 aims at universal water supply in all statutory towns, not only the 500 AMRUT cities.

st.2: India's score of 25.8 places it in the 'alarming' category.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: India's score of 25.8 falls in the 'serious' category, not 'alarming'.
Both statements are correct: current-price per capita income rises faster because it includes inflation, which constant-price figures remove.

st.3: It revised 2023-24 growth upward from 7.2% to 9.2%.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the new series revised 2023-24 growth downward, from 9.2% to 7.2%.

st.1: The four Labour Codes are the Code on Wages, the Code on Social Security, the Industrial Relations Code and the Code on Gig and Platform Workers.
st.3: The e-Shram portal is a national database of organised-sector workers.
st.4: e-Shram registration is open only to workers who are members of the EPFO or ESIC.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the fourth Code is the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code; the four consolidate 29 laws. Statement 3 is wrong: e-Shram (26 August 2021) is a database of unorganised workers. Statement 4 is wrong: EPFO and ESIC members are not eligible; each registrant gets a 12-digit UAN.

st.1: It is conducted by the National Statistical Office.
st.2: It covers establishments with 10 or more workers in nine sectors, including agriculture.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the QES is conducted by the Labour Bureau, not the NSO. Statement 2 is wrong: its nine sectors do not include agriculture.

st.2: GVA is compiled separately for four institutional sectors, one of which is cooperative societies.
st.4: The share of private corporate investment in GFCF rose to a decadal high (Aug 2026).

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the four institutional sectors are general government, public corporations, private corporations and households; cooperatives are not one. Statement 4 is wrong: the share fell to a decadal low of 33%.

st.2: The SEEA Central Framework was adopted by the World Bank in 2012.
st.3: EnviStats India is brought out annually by the Reserve Bank of India.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the SEEA Central Framework was adopted by the UN Statistical Commission. Statement 3 is wrong: EnviStats India is brought out by MoSPI, not the RBI.

st.1: The labour force counts the voluntarily unemployed as well as the involuntarily unemployed.
st.3: A person unemployed for more than twelve months is in frictional unemployment.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the labour force counts only involuntary unemployment. Statement 3 is wrong: unemployment of more than 12 months is long-term unemployment; frictional unemployment is short-term, between jobs.

st.2: The Governors of all States were its members.
st.3: Manmohan Singh was its Deputy Chairman during the Rolling Plan period of the Janata Government.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Governors were not members of the Planning Commission. Statement 3 is wrong: D.T. Lakdawala was Deputy Chairman during the Rolling Plan; Manmohan Singh held the post in 1985-87.

st.3: In plan financing, deficit financing meant borrowing from commercial banks.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: deficit financing meant borrowing from the RBI (money creation), not from commercial banks.

st.2: The declared aim in 1950 was a rapid rise in the standard of living of the urban population only.
st.4: The core element of the socialistic pattern was the nationalisation of all private firms.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 1950 aim was a rapid rise in the standard of living of the people as a whole, with employment for all. Statement 4 is wrong: the socialistic pattern did not mean nationalising all private firms; the private sector continued.

st.1: It was put forward by P.C. Mahalanobis in 'Planning for an Expanding Economy' (1956).
st.2: It held that the real constraint on expansion was the supply of capital goods.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the model was put forward by C.N. Vakil and P.R. Brahmananda. Statement 2 is wrong: it held that the real constraint was the supply of wage goods (food), not capital goods.

st.1: GDP growth was highest in 1991-92, the first year of the reforms.
st.3: Foreign exchange reserves rose from about $975 million (June 1991) to about $701.4 billion, enough for about three years of imports.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: growth was below 1% in 1991-92 and rose to 6.3% by 1994-95. Statement 3 is wrong: $701.4 billion covers about 11 months of imports.

st.2: Its members are appointed by the Chief Minister.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: SFC members are appointed by the Governor, not the Chief Minister.

st.1: It was set up after the global financial crisis of 2008.
st.3: It works under the UNEP.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the BCBS was set up at the end of 1974, after the failure of Bankhaus Herstatt. Statement 3 is wrong: it works under the Bank for International Settlements, which is not part of the UN.

st.3: The RBI's Financial Stability Report of December 2025 found banks and NBFCs failing its stress tests.
st.4: The Financial Stability Report of June 2026 flagged banks' exposure to crypto-assets.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the December 2025 report found banks and NBFCs resilient. Statement 4 is wrong: the June 2026 report flagged fintech unsecured lending, not crypto-assets.

st.1: Galloping inflation refers to single-digit inflation of 5–9% a year.
st.3: Walking or trotting inflation is faster than galloping inflation.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: galloping inflation is double- or triple-digit. Statement 3 is wrong: walking inflation (3-10%) is slower than galloping inflation.

st.1: Like the CPI, the WPI covers both goods and services.
st.2: In the WPI series with base 2011-12, primary articles had the largest weight.
st.3: In the new WPI (base 2022-23), weights are based on Gross Value Added.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the WPI covers goods only, not services. Statement 2 is wrong: manufactured products had the largest weight (64.23%). Statement 3 is wrong: the new WPI weights are based on Gross Value of Output, not GVA.

st.3: Interest payments are capital expenditure.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: interest payments are revenue expenditure.

All four statements are correct: FCI's NSSF borrowing ended in 2021-22, the FRBM caps new guarantees at 0.5% of GDP, AP's off-budget borrowing was ₹1.28 lakh crore in March 2023, and the 16th FC wants it brought on-budget.

st.1: States passed Fiscal Responsibility Laws after the Planning Commission linked debt relief (Debt Consolidation and Relief Facility) to them.
st.2: The Union FRBM Act, 2003 applies directly to the States.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: it was the Twelfth Finance Commission that linked the DCRF to fiscal responsibility laws. Statement 2 is wrong: the Union FRBM Act binds only the Centre; States passed their own laws.

st.1: It recommended a narrower deficit definition that leaves out off-budget borrowing.
st.3: It described State fiscal rules as strictly enforced.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: it recommended a wider deficit definition that includes off-budget borrowing. Statement 3 is wrong: it described State fiscal rules as 'effectively unenforced'.

st.1: It is a U-shaped curve, with maximum tax revenue at both 0% and 100% tax rates.
st.2: The term 'Laffer curve' was coined by Arthur Laffer himself in 1974.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: it is an inverted-U curve, with zero revenue at 0% and 100%. Statement 2 is wrong: the term was coined by Jude Wanniski in 1974, not by Laffer.

st.3: Long-term capital gains are taxed at 20%, the same rate as short-term gains on listed equity (as of August 2026).
st.4: Rural agricultural land is a capital asset under the Income-tax Act.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: long-term capital gains are taxed at 12.5% (as of August 2026). Statement 4 is wrong: rural agricultural land is not a capital asset.

st.2: A composition dealer can claim input tax credit.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: a composition dealer cannot claim input tax credit.

st.2: In June 1966 the rupee was devalued under the Janata Government.
st.3: The July 1991 devaluation was carried out in a single step.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the June 1966 devaluation (₹4.76 to ₹7.50) was under Indira Gandhi's Congress Government. Statement 3 is wrong: the 1991 devaluation came in two steps, on 1 and 3 July.

st.2: The average operational holding has risen since the 10th Agriculture Census.
st.4: Srikakulam had the smallest average holding.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the average holding fell from 0.94 ha to 0.86 ha. Statement 4 is wrong: Visakhapatnam (0.40 ha), not Srikakulam, had the smallest average holding.

st.3: Kisan Credit Cards are issued by NABARD directly to farmers.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: KCCs are issued by banks (commercial, regional rural and cooperative), not by NABARD directly.

st.2: In the State, SERP handles urban SHGs and MEPMA handles rural SHGs.
st.3: SHG members must each have an individual CIBIL credit history to get bank linkage.
st.4: Under MEPMA, SHGs must be registered before bank linkage.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: SERP is rural and MEPMA urban. Statement 3 is wrong: SHG members often lack individual CIBIL histories, and linkage does not need them. Statement 4 is wrong: SHGs need no registration; MEPMA linkage goes up to Rs 20 lakh.

st.3: They also apply to loans sanctioned before 1 January 2027.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Directions apply only to loans from 1 January 2027.

st.2: The Shanta Kumar High Level Committee recommended extending PDS coverage to 90 per cent of the population.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Shanta Kumar Committee (which put leakage at about 46%) recommended cutting NFSA coverage from 67% to about 40%.

st.2: It seeks to bring more sectors under the public sector.
st.3: It seeks to raise the share of government equity in CPSEs.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: disinvestment seeks to improve PSU efficiency, not to widen the public sector. Statement 3 is wrong: it reduces, not raises, the government's equity in CPSEs.

st.1: In 2023-24, AP's real growth (6.18%) was higher than India's (8.2%).
st.3: In 2025-26 (FAE) AP grew faster than India only at current prices.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: AP's 6.18% was lower than India's 8.2% in 2023-24. Statement 3 is wrong: in 2025-26 AP grew faster than India at both current and constant prices.

st.3: Universal Basic Income is one of the 10 Padi Sutralu of Swarna Andhra.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Universal Basic Income is not one of the 10 Padi Sutralu; they begin with Zero Poverty.

st.2: It came into force on 1 July 2017 for all goods, including petroleum crude.
st.3: GST compensation to States was promised for ten years.
st.4: GST Council decisions need a three-fourths majority, with the Centre's vote carrying two-thirds of the weight.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: GST came into force on 1 July 2017, but petroleum crude and fuels are still outside it. Statement 3 is wrong: compensation was promised for five years, to June 2022. Statement 4 is wrong: the Centre's vote carries one-third of the weight and the States' two-thirds.

st.2: It was implemented by the NDDB, which was set up in 1965 at Karnal.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the NDDB was set up in 1965 at Anand, not Karnal.

st.2: The 21st Livestock Census covered only cattle and buffaloes.
st.3: The 21st Livestock Census covered only exotic and crossbred breeds.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 21st Census covered 16 species. Statement 3 is wrong: it covered 219 indigenous breeds.

st.2: 16.2% of APIIC plots were earmarked for MSMEs.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 16.2% share of APIIC plots was for SC entrepreneurs; MSMEs got 33% of the land.

st.2: SEZs have received more than half of India's FDI inflows.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: SEZs have received less than 3% of India's FDI.

st.2: APIIC is its executing agency.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the executing agency is the Department of Industries and Commerce; APIIC is one of the four PIUs.

st.2: Kakinada SEZ is an IT/ITES SEZ.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Kakinada SEZ is a multi-product SEZ; the IT/ITES SEZ is at Visakhapatnam.

st.2: Its ₹10,000 crore refinance window is provided through NABARD.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the ₹10,000 crore refinance window is through SIDBI, not NABARD.

st.1: Article 48A is a Fundamental Duty of the citizen.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Article 48A is a Directive Principle; the citizen's duty is Article 51A(g).

st.3: Its beneficiaries were identified from Census 2011 income declarations.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: beneficiaries were identified from the deprivation criteria of SECC 2011, not Census income declarations.

st.3: ABDM is implemented by the ICMR.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: ABDM (announced as NDHM on 15 August 2020) is implemented by the National Health Authority.

st.2: The first BRIC Summit was held in Brazil.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the first BRIC Summit was held in 2009 at Yekaterinburg, Russia.

st.2: The Earth moves fastest at perihelion.

x: All three statements are correct: the Earth is about 152 million km away at aphelion, moves fastest at perihelion, and perihelion (early January) falls in the northern winter.

st.2: Uranus and Neptune are called ice giants.

x: All three statements are correct: the four inner planets lie inside the asteroid belt, Uranus and Neptune are ice giants (Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants), and Mars is the outermost inner planet.

st.3: Uzbekistan and Liechtenstein are the doubly landlocked countries.

st.2: The Dardanelles connects the Black Sea with the Aegean Sea.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Dardanelles connects the Sea of Marmara (not the Black Sea) with the Aegean.

st.3: In Andhra Pradesh, coastal Visakhapatnam and Kakinada have a higher daily range than interior Rayalaseema.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: coastal Visakhapatnam and Kakinada have a small daily range because of sea breezes; interior Rayalaseema has the higher range.

st.3: Of India's utilisable water resources of 1,139 BCM, groundwater accounts for the larger share.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: surface water (690 BCM) is the larger share; groundwater is 449 BCM.

st.2: India's 'zero casualty' approach to cyclones has been followed since Cyclone Phailin (2013).

x: All four statements are correct: Phailin (2013) saw over a million evacuated and began the 'zero casualty' approach, Michaung (2023) hit AP and flooded Chennai, and Operation Sagar Bandhu helped Sri Lanka after Cyclone Ditwah.

st.2: The atmospheric counterpart of El Nino is the Southern Oscillation.
st.3: El Nino can also develop in the Indian Ocean and the Bay of Bengal.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: El Nino develops only in the Pacific Ocean, not in the Indian Ocean or the Bay of Bengal.

st.2: It bounds Palk Bay in the south.

st.2: Kolleru lies between the Godavari and the Krishna.
st.3: Pulicat is India's largest brackish-water lagoon.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Chilika is India's largest brackish-water lagoon; Pulicat is the second largest.

st.2: The Papikonda hills form the gorge of the Godavari.

x: All four statements are correct: Araku is the 'Ooty of AP', the Papikondalu form the Godavari gorge (the Erramala is the Krishna–Penna divide), Seshachalam is known for red sanders, and the Biligirirangans are in Karnataka.

st.1: The Thal Ghat links Mumbai with Pune.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Thal Ghat links Mumbai with Nashik; the Bhor Ghat links Mumbai with Pune.

st.2: Lambasingi, the coldest place of Andhra Pradesh, is in Tirupati district.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Lambasingi is in Alluri Sitarama Raju district, not Tirupati district.

st.3: Their winter rain in the north-western plains increases from west to east.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: western-disturbance rain in the north-western plains decreases from west to east.

st.3: The IMD Cyclone Warning Centre of Andhra Pradesh is at Kakinada.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the IMD Cyclone Warning Centre of AP is at Visakhapatnam, not Kakinada.

st.2: The Coromandel coast receives north-east monsoon rain.

x: All three statements are correct: Tamil Nadu gets the most north-east monsoon rain, the Coromandel coast receives it, and AP gets about one-third of its rain in October–December.

st.2: Planting Eucalyptus is a drought-prevention measure.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Eucalyptus draws heavily on groundwater, so planting it is not a drought-prevention measure.

st.1: The Sahibi is a south-flowing river.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Sahibi flows north from the Aravallis towards Haryana and the Yamuna.

st.3: Jharkhand is one of the States of the Godavari basin.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Jharkhand is not a Godavari basin State; the basin covers Maharashtra, Telangana, AP, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, MP, Karnataka and Puducherry.

st.1: Much of Andhra Pradesh lies on granitoid-gneiss bedrock.

x: All three statements are correct: much of AP lies on granitoid-gneiss, deltaic and coastal alluvium covers about 5–6%, and laterite is the smallest of the four main soils (about 1%).

st.2: Red sanders is listed in Schedule IV of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

x: All four statements are correct: red sanders is IUCN Endangered, in Schedule IV of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, in CITES Appendix II, and endemic to the Seshachalam, Palakonda and Veligonda ranges.

st.4: As per ISFR 2023, the tree cover of Andhra Pradesh is 8,351.62 sq km.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: 8,351.62 sq km is AP's scrub, which is not forest; its tree cover is 5,340.02 sq km.

st.2: The Western Ghats and Nilgiris are landslide-prone because of steep slopes and heavy monsoon rain.
st.3: Increased forestation in hilly areas is a cause of landslides.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: deforestation, not forestation, is a cause of landslides in hilly areas.

st.2: India's indigenous GLOF alert system was tested at Sissu in Uttarakhand.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the indigenous GLOF alert system was tested at Sissu in Himachal Pradesh, not Uttarakhand.

st.1: 'Prakampana', the super-cyclone exercise at Visakhapatnam, was conducted by the Western Naval Command.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: 'Prakampana' at Visakhapatnam was conducted by the Eastern Naval Command.

st.4: The annual 61-day ban on mechanised fishing applies in the EEZ (12–200 nm), a Central subject.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the 61-day ban applies in territorial waters (0–12 nm), a State subject.

st.2: Under PMMSY the subsidy is 60% for general beneficiaries and 40% for women, SC and ST.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the PMMSY subsidy is 40% for general beneficiaries and 60% for women, SC and ST.

st.4: The Upper Sileru pumped storage project stores night-time power to meet daytime peaks.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: pumped storage such as Upper Sileru (1,350 MW) stores surplus daytime (solar) power to meet night peaks.

st.2: Steel accounts for about 10–12% of India's CO2 emissions.

x: All three statements are correct: Indian steel emits about 2.54 t CO2 per tonne against 1.9 worldwide, it accounts for about 10–12% of India's CO2, and a draft notification brings it under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme.

st.2: The silk weavers came mainly from the Devanga and Padmasali communities.

x: All three statements are correct: silks were luxury goods, weavers came from the Devanga, Padmasali and other communities, and the industry declined in the 19th century under Chinese and Japanese competition.

st.3: The East-West corridor, from Silchar to Porbandar, is longer than the North-South corridor.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the East-West corridor (about 3,640 km through 7 States) is shorter than the North-South corridor.

st.2: YSR Kadapa district stood first in India in the Basic Infrastructure theme.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Alluri Sitarama Raju, not YSR Kadapa, stood first in the Basic Infrastructure theme.

st.3: Bihar ranked third among States both in population and in area.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Bihar was third in population but not in area.

st.2: The term 'Shrinconomics' for the fall in fertility was used by the Andhra Pradesh Health Minister on 1 April 2026.

x: All three statements are correct: 'demographic winter' means sub-2.1 fertility and decline, 'Shrinconomics' was used by the AP Health Minister on 1 April 2026, and the Economic Survey 2018-19 warned of a 'demographic nightmare'.

st.2: The urban migration rate was lower than the rural migration rate.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the urban migration rate was higher than the rural rate.

st.2: The Ol Chiki script of Santhali was devised by Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy in 1925.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Ol Chiki was devised by Pandit Raghunath Murmu in 1925, not by Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy.

st.3: An atoll encloses a lagoon that has central land.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: an atoll encloses a lagoon without central land.

st.1: Nagarjunasagar–Srisailam Tiger Reserve lies in both Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Nagarjunasagar–Srisailam Tiger Reserve lies only in AP; the Telangana part is the Amrabad Tiger Reserve.

st.3: Gundla Brahmeswaram WLS lies wholly in Kadapa district.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Gundla Brahmeswaram WLS (notified 1990) lies in Kurnool (Nandyal) and Prakasam districts.

st.3: In Andhra Pradesh, Rajiv Gandhi WLS spans Kadapa, Annamayya and Tirupati districts.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Rajiv Gandhi WLS lies in Nandyal, Prakasam and Palnadu districts; the Rajiv Gandhi National Park is in Kadapa.

st.3: Tamil Nadu has the lowest natural growth rate.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Kerala (3.9 per 1,000), not Tamil Nadu, has the lowest natural growth rate.

st.2: Mediterranean agricultural regions receive most of their rain in summer.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Mediterranean regions get most of their rain in winter; summers are dry.

st.2: The S&T Policy 2003 aimed at GERD of 2% of GDP, to be met wholly from public spending.
st.3: The 24 May 2026 recommendations proposed a single fellowship called 'Vigyan Dhara'.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2003 policy wanted GERD of 2% of GDP by the end of the Tenth Plan, with private spending matching public. Statement 3 is wrong: the 24 May 2026 recommendations proposed a single fellowship called 'Vigyan Nidhi'.

st.4: The Draft STIP 2020 followed a top-down design drafted by the DST alone.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the Draft STIP 2020, India's fifth policy, used a decentralised, bottom-up, inclusive design.

st.3: PURSE – Programme for University Research and Science Education

x: Items 1 and 2 are correct. Item 3 is wrong: PURSE stands for Promotion of University Research and Scientific Excellence.

st.3: The IT Act, 2000 gave legal basis to e-records but not to digital signatures.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the IT Act, 2000 gave legal basis to both e-records and digital signatures (it was amended in 2008).

st.3: The Lepakshi Space City is meant to host a second spaceport.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Lepakshi Space City is meant for R&D; Sriharikota remains the only spaceport.

st.1: A fuel cell generates electricity by burning hydrogen.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: a fuel cell makes electricity by an electrochemical reaction, without burning hydrogen.

st.1: ISO 10218 sets safety norms for surgical robots.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: ISO 10218 sets safety norms for industrial robots, not surgical robots.

st.2: BharatNet is funded by the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: BharatNet is funded by the Universal Service Obligation Fund (now Digital Bharat Nidhi), not the NIIF.

st.3: Hanooman (May 2024) is linked to the BharatGPT group led by IIT Delhi.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the BharatGPT group behind Hanooman is led by IIT Bombay, not IIT Delhi.
All three statements are correct: the VELC was built by the IIA, the SUIT by IUCAA, and Aditya-L1 carries seven payloads (four remote-sensing, three in-situ).

st.2: The impact site is named Shiv Shakti Point.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Moon Impact Probe site is Jawahar Point; Shiv Shakti Point is Chandrayaan-3's landing site.

st.2: Belarus was its first foreign buyer after Russia.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: China, not Belarus, was the first foreign buyer of the S-400.

st.2: Nag and Akash were developed by ISRO under the programme.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Nag, Akash and the other IGMDP missiles were developed by DRDO, not ISRO.

st.3: In May 1992 the USA put DRDO on hold under the MTCR.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the May 1992 US sanctions over the cryogenic deal were on ISRO and Glavkosmos, not DRDO.

st.3: AP FiberNet reached 4,000+ tribal hamlets in the Western Ghats.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: AP FiberNet reached 4,000+ tribal hamlets in the Eastern Ghats, not the Western Ghats.

st.1: Mobile-Aadhaar linking, mandated in 2017, was upheld by the Supreme Court in September 2018.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: mobile-Aadhaar linking, mandated in 2017, was struck down by the Supreme Court in September 2018.

All three statements are correct: RTGS was formed on 6 September 2017 under the CM with its State Centre at Velagapudi, its dashboards draw on AWARE, and it was revived from 2024 as an AI platform with 59 Chief Data Officers.

st.2: It became a statutory body under Section 70A of the IT Act.
st.4: Under the same Directions, government bodies are exempt from reporting cyber incidents.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: CERT-In is statutory under Section 70B (Section 70A is the NCIIPC). Statement 4 is wrong: the Directions cover government bodies too; VPN providers must keep data for 5 years.

st.3: Environment (Protection) Act, 1986

x: Items 1 and 2 are correct. Item 3 is wrong: the SHANTI Act repealed the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the CLND Act, 2010, not the Environment (Protection) Act.

st.2: Heavy water was discovered by H.C. Urey, who received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1934 for it.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: H.C. Urey received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry, not Physics, in 1934.

st.3: During the 2026 gas crisis, the Strait of Malacca was identified as the main risk to India's LPG supplies.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Strait of Hormuz, not Malacca, was the main risk to India's LPG supplies in 2026.

st.2: It has fallen since 2013-14.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: per capita consumption rose from 957 kWh in 2013-14 to 1,460 kWh in 2024-25.

st.2: India's first geothermal power project at Puga, Ladakh was taken up by NTPC.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Puga geothermal project was taken up by ONGC, not NTPC.

st.3: The CAFE III targets are about 21% stricter than the September 2025 proposal.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the CAFE III targets are about 21% relaxed, not stricter, than the September 2025 proposal.

st.1: The Department of Hydro and Renewable Energy (DHRE), IIT Roorkee, is an institution under MNRE.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: DHRE, IIT Roorkee supports small hydro but is not an institution under MNRE.

st.1: Andhra Pradesh has the largest share (23.70%) of India's renewable-energy potential.

x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Rajasthan has the largest share (23.70%) of India's RE potential; AP has 9.10%.

st.3: Amensalism is a +/+ interaction.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: amensalism is a −/0 interaction; +/+ is mutualism.

st.1: The term 'biological diversity' was coined by Norman Myers.
st.3: To qualify as a hotspot, a region must have at least 1,500 endemic animal species.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: 'biological diversity' was coined by Raymond F. Dasmann. Statement 3 is wrong: the test is at least 1,500 endemic vascular plants and at least 70% of habitat lost.

st.3: Thailand is one of the megadiverse countries.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Thailand is not one of the 17 megadiverse countries.

st.2: The leatherback turtle is Critically Endangered.
st.3: The tiger is listed as Critically Endangered.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the leatherback turtle is Vulnerable. Statement 3 is wrong: the tiger is Endangered, not Critically Endangered.

st.3: Karnataka recorded the largest loss of forest cover.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Madhya Pradesh recorded the largest loss of forest cover, with Karnataka next.

st.2: The Watershed Development Component of PMKSY follows a 'valley to ridge' approach.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the PMKSY watershed component follows a 'ridge to valley' approach.

st.3: Ex-situ conservation can save the whole ecosystem, though it needs space and money.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: ex-situ conservation saves species or genes outside their habitat; only in-situ conservation saves the whole ecosystem.

st.2: It provided for Conservation Reserves, which are declared on private or community land.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Conservation Reserves are on government land; Community Reserves are on private or community land.

st.3: The cement sector is the largest source of India's GHG emissions.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the energy sector (mainly coal power) is India's largest GHG source; cement is a smaller share.

st.3: Its main industrial polluter is a cement plant.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the main industrial polluter is Andhra Paper Ltd, a paper mill, not a cement plant.

st.1: Category A projects are exempt from public hearing.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Category A projects are not exempt from public hearing; B2 projects and defence or strategic projects are.

st.3: It is the convention on the control of persistent organic pollutants.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Minamata deals with man-made mercury emissions; persistent organic pollutants are covered by the Stockholm Convention.

st.1: Its Just Transition Fund is meant to protect and restore ecosystems.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Just Transition Fund supports affected regions; protecting and restoring ecosystems is the Biodiversity Strategy's job.

st.2: Direct-seeded rice is promoted along with zero-till wheat under PM-KUSUM.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: direct-seeded rice with zero-till wheat is promoted under NICRA, not PM-KUSUM (a solar-pump scheme).

st.2: Corals and bivalve larvae use calcite, which is less soluble than aragonite, and so are less sensitive to acidification.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: corals and bivalve larvae use aragonite, which is more soluble than calcite, so they are more sensitive to acidification.

st.2: The secretariat of the Global Biofuels Alliance is at Washington DC.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Global Biofuels Alliance secretariat is at New Delhi, not Washington DC.

st.2: The obligated entities under the CCTS are mainly in the IT and banking sectors.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 282 obligated entities are in aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali, pulp and paper and similar industries.

st.2: Denmark was ranked first in the Sustainable Development Report 2026.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Finland was first in the SDR 2026, with Sweden and Denmark next.

st.3: It gave the first definition of sustainable development.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the first widely accepted definition of sustainable development came from the Brundtland Report (1987).

st.2: Cancer is a nationally notifiable disease.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: cancer is not a nationally notifiable disease; 17 States have notified it.

st.2: A high ratio of communicable-disease DALYs to NCD and injury DALYs indicates a high ETL.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: a low ratio of communicable to NCD and injury DALYs indicates a high ETL.

st.3: A burning glass diverges the sun's rays.
st.4: Myopia is corrected with a concave lens of positive power.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: a burning glass (convex lens) converges the sun's rays. Statement 4 is wrong: myopia is corrected with a concave lens of negative power.

st.2: NAL's aircraft Saras is named after the Great Indian Bustard.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Saras is named after the Sarus crane, not the Great Indian Bustard.

st.3: It is located at Ahmedabad.
st.4: Its Festival of Innovation (FOIN) is held at Vigyan Bhawan.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: NIF-India is at Gandhinagar, not Ahmedabad. Statement 4 is wrong: FOIN is held at Rashtrapati Bhavan.

st.2: It named AIIMS, New Delhi, to coordinate the BRICS mental-health centres.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: NIMHANS, not AIIMS New Delhi, is to coordinate the BRICS mental-health centres.

st.2: The Ramsar Convention was adopted on 2 February 1971 at Ramsar, Iraq.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Ramsar is in Iran, not Iraq.

st.3: India–France ties were raised to a Special Global Strategic Partnership at the Nice meeting of June 2026.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Special Global Strategic Partnership was announced at Mumbai on 17 February 2026; Nice (June 2026) approved the Innovation Roadmap.

st.4: The Global Methane Pledge was launched at COP27 in Sharm el-Sheikh.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the Global Methane Pledge was launched at COP26, Glasgow (2021), to cut methane 30% by 2030.

st.2: Nigeria is a member of the G20.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Nigeria is not a G20 member; South Africa is the African member country, besides the African Union.

st.3: The Bharat 6G Alliance partnered with the University of Helsinki.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Bharat 6G Alliance partnered with the University of Oulu, not Helsinki.

st.2: The United States is to contribute more than half of the $70 billion.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the US is to give $10 billion, well under half of the pledged $70 billion.

st.3: Madagascar is a member of ECOWAS.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Madagascar belongs to SADC, not ECOWAS (a West African bloc).

st.3: India, Brazil and Indonesia formed the Digital Innovation Alliance.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Digital Innovation Alliance is of India, Brazil and South Africa, not Indonesia.

st.3: Its theme was 'One Earth, One Family, One Future'.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: 'One Earth, One Family, One Future' was the theme of India's 2023 summit; Johannesburg's was 'Solidarity, Equality, Sustainability'.

st.2: The Board of Governors runs the daily operations of the institutions.
st.4: The World Bank is headed by Kristalina Georgieva.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Board of Governors has no executive authority over daily operations. Statement 4 is wrong: the World Bank is headed by Ajay Banga; Kristalina Georgieva heads the IMF.

st.2: The members for the 2028–29 seat will be elected by the Security Council itself.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: non-permanent members are elected by the UN General Assembly; the 2028–29 election is in June 2027.

st.3: Venezuela gave its notice of withdrawal to the ICC Prosecutor.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: under Article 127 notice of withdrawal goes to the UN Secretary-General, not the ICC Prosecutor (Venezuela had joined in 2002).

st.2: Lucknow became India's first UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy in 2025.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Lucknow (2025) was not India's first City of Gastronomy; Hyderabad was named earlier.

st.3: The EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) applies only to timber and wood products.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the EUDR covers cattle, cocoa, coffee, oil palm, rubber and soya as well as wood (deforestation after 2020).

st.4: The Pandemic Agreement opened for signature before its PABS annex was adopted.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the Agreement opens for signature only after the PABS annex is adopted, and the annex is still pending.

st.3: The Exploration Museum with an Astronaut Monument to Apollo astronauts is in Reykjavik.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Exploration Museum with the Astronaut Monument is at Husavik, not Reykjavik.

st.2: The IMO supported the fee, noting a legal basis for tolls on international straits.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the IMO opposed the fee, saying there is no legal basis for tolls on international straits.

st.2: IRIS Dena was returning from the International Fleet Review 2026 at Kochi when it was sunk.
st.3: India's Shahid Beheshti terminal at Chabahar was destroyed in the strikes of July 2026.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: IRIS Dena was returning from the International Fleet Review 2026 at Visakhapatnam, not Kochi. Statement 3 is wrong: India's Shahid Beheshti terminal was undamaged in the July 2026 strikes.

st.1: E5 series Shinkansen was chosen at the 2025 summit for the Mumbai–Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail.
st.4: India runs a trade surplus with Japan.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the E10 series Shinkansen was chosen for the Mumbai–Ahmedabad line. Statement 4 is wrong: India runs a trade deficit with Japan.

st.2: The 1996 Ganga Water Sharing Treaty concerns sharing of water at the Teesta barrage.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 1996 treaty concerns Ganga water at Farakka; the Teesta is a separate dispute.

st.1: The snapback was triggered by Russia and China under the JCPOA.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the snapback was triggered by the E3 (UK, France and Germany), not by Russia and China.

st.3: Tarique Rahman became Prime Minister of Nepal.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Tarique Rahman of the BNP became Prime Minister of Bangladesh, not Nepal.

st.2: NGOPV 'Srishti' (Yard 1283) was launched at GRSE, Kolkata, on 27 October 2026.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: NGOPV 'Srishti' was launched at Goa Shipyard, not GRSE.

st.1: It was built by Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Samarthak was built by L&T at Kattupalli, not by Mazagon Dock.

st.3: Data centres were put in the Harmonised List of Infrastructure in Budget 2022–23.
st.4: The TCS–HyperVault campus, billed as India's largest, is at Visakhapatnam.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the TCS–HyperVault campus is at Hyderabad Future City, not Visakhapatnam.

st.1: Semicon 2.0 has an outlay of ₹1,27,500 crore.
st.2: Semicon 2.0 leaves out chip design and talent and funds only fabs.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Semicon 2.0 has six pillars – Design, Machines and Materials, Fabs, Packaging, Research and Talent.

st.3: It spreads mainly through airborne transmission.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Ebola spreads through direct contact with body fluids, not mainly through the air.

st.1: IBM aims at a fault-tolerant quantum computer by 2029, based on trapped-ion qubits.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: IBM's 2029 fault-tolerant machine is based on superconducting qubits, not trapped ions.

st.3: INAS 330 'The Harpoons', decommissioned after 55 years, flew Chetak helicopters.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: INAS 330 'The Harpoons' flew Sea King Mk 42B helicopters, not Chetaks.

st.1: Pregabalin has been moved from Schedule H1 to Schedule H of the Drugs Rules, 1945.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: pregabalin was moved from Schedule H to the stricter Schedule H1.

st.2: Mahendragiri, delivered by MDL on 30 April 2026, is the last of the seven Project 17A frigates.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Mahendragiri is the sixth P-17A frigate; the seventh, Vindhyagiri, is being built at GRSE.

st.3: The Semiconductor Investors Support Portal (26 May 2026) was launched by NITI Aayog.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Semiconductor Investors Support Portal was launched by the ISM under MeitY, not NITI Aayog.

st.2: In a lithium-ion cell, LiFePO4 is used as the anode.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: in a lithium-ion cell LiFePO4 is the cathode, not the anode.

st.1: Heron Mk II is a MALE UAV made by Elbit Systems.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Heron Mk II is made by Israel Aerospace Industries, not Elbit Systems.

st.2: The R78C malaria vaccine targets the liver-stage antigens RIPR and CyPRA.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: R78C targets the blood-stage antigens RIPR and CyPRA, not liver-stage ones.

st.1: The Zoological Survey of India was established before the Botanical Survey of India.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Botanical Survey (1890) came before the Zoological Survey (1916).

st.2: The Yana Caves near Gokarna, declared on 13 April 2026, lie in the Eastern Ghats.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Yana Caves near Gokarna lie in the Western Ghats.

st.2: The Chicxulub crater, formed about 66 million years ago, is in Canada.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Chicxulub crater is in Mexico, not Canada.

st.3: India ranked 23rd in the Climate Change Performance Index 2026, an improvement of 13 places.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: India ranked 23rd in the CCPI 2026, down 13 places.

st.2: Andhra Pradesh and Telangana were praised for the fastest disbursement of incentives.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Andhra Pradesh and Telangana were flagged for slow incentive disbursement.

st.1: The 2019 NIA Amendment allowed individuals to be designated as terrorists.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: designation of individuals as terrorists came through the 2019 UAPA Amendment; the NIA Amendment covered offences abroad.

st.1: At the end of 2025 refugees (41.6 million) outnumbered internally displaced persons.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: IDPs (68.6 million) far outnumbered refugees (41.6 million).

st.2: It is published by the World Bank.
